reason: E1 directly supports that specific pair interactions lead to chemical clustering and short-range order in Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni, and E2 links short-range order between Al and Ni/Co to phase formation, but neither provides evidence that such order pins the structure against segregation or that reducing pair interactions reduces clustering, leaving several mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: Specific favorable atomic pair interactions induce short-range chemical order in HEAs
This short-range order pins the structure and suppresses phase segregation at high temperature
Reducing strong pair interactions (e.g., by compositional adjustment) will diminish local clustering
High configurational entropy competes with enthalpic ordering tendencies
Nanoscale ordered domains act as pinning centers to maintain single-phase structure
